A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Live Avatar work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables, figures and algorithms can be matched despite reflow and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v5 reports original benchmark comparisons, component ablations, 10,000-second generation experiments and a 20-participant user study, including Tables 2–11.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experiments, ablations, long-horizon results and user-study outcomes in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The two-stage training procedure, motion-frame scaffolding, History Corrupt, Adaptive Attention Sink, Rolling RoPE and TPP remain unchanged. Appendix Algorithms 1–4 also match; the increased emphasis on noisy history does not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain AVSpeech training and held-out evaluation, GenBench-ShortVideo and LongVideo, the looped-audio 10,000-second test and the user study. Removing the opening teaser does not establish any change to the datasets or scenarios actually evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in Tables 2, 8 and 9: Ditto, EchoMimic-V2, Hallo3, StableAvatar, OmniAvatar and WanS2V. Both versions exclude EchoMimic-V2 from the long-video comparison and retain the same ablation comparators.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1–5.3 and Appendices D–F change the reported training and benchmarking hardware from H800 to H100. Budgets, splits, metrics and evaluation procedures otherwise remain unchanged. This establishes a reported setting revision, not that experiments were rerun. The new introductory claim of approximately 3-second training conflicts with the retained 5-second description in Appendix C.1.

E4.justification: Removing v5 Figure 1 removes two illustrative long-horizon generation cases, including an anthropomorphic fire example. This slightly reduces qualitative case evidence. The structured ablations, 10,000-second stress analysis, user study and other qualitative comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged: neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both retain the same user-study averaging and normalized mean ratings.

E6.justification: Tables 2–11 and retained result plots match, including 45.2 FPS and 1.21-second TTFF. The limited deletion is v5 Figure 1's additional qualitative sequences and its 20-FPS annotation. The hardware relabeling does not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The flow-matching, DMD and block-conditioning formulations in Equations 1–5 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The introduction now explicitly claims train-short-infer-long generation from approximately 3-second training clips; v5's explicit duration was 5 seconds in Appendix C.1, which v6 retains. The headline efficiency claim changes hardware to H100. The broader 14B streaming, long-horizon and GenBench contributions remain, although GenBench is omitted from the revised abstract.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, result interpretations, the static-scene restriction and approximately 3-second interaction-latency limitation remain. The new throughput-only definition of real-time clarifies the distinction already conveyed by v5's FPS threshold and explicit limitation on bidirectional real-time interaction.

D1.justification: Hardware documentation changes from H800 to H100. v6 also removes both promises to release GenBench and evaluation scripts in the camera-ready version, while retaining the project link, implementation recipes and pseudocode. This removes stated release information without establishing any actual change in resource availability.

R1.justification: The same 58 references and substantive related-work discussion are retained. Relationships to Self-Forcing, LongLive, prior avatar methods and diffusion distillation are unchanged.

P1.justification: v6 rewrites the abstract and parts of the introduction, reverses the order of the two motivating challenges and foregrounds noisy-history conditioning. It also updates author information, adds keywords, fixes running headers and places Appendix G–H after the algorithms. Most technical prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The opening teaser is removed, and the remaining figures are renumbered and sometimes relocated or resized. Tables retain their structure, and retained graphics show the same content. Algorithm placement changes, leaving v6 page 30 blank apart from its header.

improvement.justification: The revised framing and explicit throughput definition improve clarity, but v6 introduces a conflict between approximately 3-second training in the introduction and exclusive 5-second training in Appendix C.1. It also removes the GenBench/script release commitment without replacement access information. These limited losses in consistency and access documentation outweigh the presentation refinements; the experimental evidence is otherwise retained.
